# AID Defence · DESIGN (DRAFT)

> **DRAFT. No visual decisions have been made.** The YAML block above is generated from `tokens/` by
> `npm run build` and holds placeholder values only. Prose below records what is confirmed and what is open.
> Format: Google Labs DESIGN.md (YAML tokens + prose, canonical section order, extra sections allowed).

## Overview
AID Defence makes specialised defence products: NAVIC CMS (convoy management; Lighthouse is its software),
ADS (anti-drone system), AI IoT Bridge, OBD. The brand is **mature, very clear, no nonsense, on point**, and
discreet: it shows a glimpse of the problem and the approach, then invites a private conversation. Audiences
include senior, non-technical officers. A separate identity: people outside defence need never meet it.

## Colors
Placeholder only: a deepened blue and a sand accent, labelled `placeholder-*` in `tokens/palette.tokens.json`.
- Use semantic roles, never palette steps.
- Protected and identical everywhere: `status.*` (six levels: off, standby, normal, caution, serious, critical),
  `focus.*`, and this brand's opt-in modules `symbology.*` and `classification.*`. Never restyle them.
- Classification banner colours and levels are placeholders: the customer-mandated scheme must replace them.

## Typography
One Google Fonts sans family shared across the group (decided); family not chosen yet. Operator UI uses the
`code` role (mono) for coordinates, timestamps and telemetry.

## Layout
12-column grid, 4px base. Operator consoles (Lighthouse) use `data-density="compact"`; marketing and
collateral use comfortable. Placeholder values.

## Elevation & Depth
Open. Night mode should rely on borders, not shadows.

## Shapes
Shared core radii: `radius.control`, `radius.container`, `radius.pill`.

## Components
Core reference components, plus the classification banner (`.aid-classification[data-level]`) and status pill
(`.aid-status[data-status]`). Lighthouse needs tactical symbology: token placeholders exist; symbol set open.

## Do's and Don'ts
- Do explain technical products so a senior non-technical officer understands them in one read.
- Do lead with the problem and approach; keep specifics for the private conversation.
- Don't show real sites, kit, units, locations or anything sensitive. Never lead with capability claims.
- Don't use hex values outside `tokens/`, and never change status, symbology or classification colours.

## Modes
Light and dark for documents and web; **night** for Lighthouse and low-light operation. Night mode is
brand-immune by design (low luminance, red-shifted) to protect dark adaptation.

## Imagery
AI imagery by default; real kit and sites cannot be shown. Each generated image has a prompt sidecar `.md`.
Imagery direction: open.

## Motion
Minimal and functional. Every animated component designs a reduced-motion state.
